name: Haditha–Kirkuk Oil Pipeline (Basra–Ceyhan corridor connector)

values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: No route drawn or chosen. Iraq's cabinet approved (5 Jul 2026) a non-binding heads-of-agreement + NDA for a Chevron/Capital TI/UCC Holding consortium (via Basra Oil Co.) to run feasibility studies comparing two rival corridors out of Haditha: 'Route 1' Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan (this row — the missing Haditha-to-Kirkuk link that would tie existing P0544 Basra-Haditha to existing P0547 Kirkuk-Ceyhan) vs 'Route 2' Basra-Haditha-Baniyas (bypasses Kirkuk entirely, different corridor). Studies due end-2026; construction start not before 2027 at earliest. Endpoints (Haditha, Kirkuk) are named in multiple sources but no map/GIS/coordinates exist yet — point-to-point only, and even that is provisional pending the route choice.

researcher_notes:
PASSES add-threshold: (a) sponsor — Chevron/Capital TI (US)/UCC Holding (Qatar) consortium, contracted via Basra Oil Co.; (b) country+endpoints — Iraq, Haditha to Kirkuk (the specific missing link identified by name in agbi's 'Route 1: Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan' and al-monitor's 'pipeline from southern Iraq to Kirkuk in the north'); (c) concrete step — Iraq's cabinet approved (5 Jul 2026) a heads-of-agreement + NDA with the consortium for feasibility studies, reported independently by pipeline-journal.net, iraqinews.com (x2 separate articles), agbi.com, energynow.com and al-monitor.com — treated as MOU-equivalent (a formally signed, cabinet-ratified preliminary agreement), not mere rumor.

RE-CHECKED vs existing rows first (discovery_context.json, 86 existing Iraq oil rows): confirmed NO existing row covers a Haditha-to-Kirkuk segment. P0544 (Basra-Aqaba Oil Pipeline > Basra-Haditha segment, construction) ends at Haditha; P5240 (Haditha-Aqaba segment, proposed) continues WEST to Jordan; P0547 (Kirkuk-Ceyhan Oil Pipeline, operating) starts at Kirkuk and runs to Turkey; none of the Kirkuk-Baniyas rows (P0546/P5277-79/P7913) touch Haditha. The Haditha→Kirkuk gap genuinely has no roster PID — this is a new_row, not matched_existing.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT — route not fixed: the same 5 Jul 2026 heads-of-agreement covers feasibility studies for TWO rival corridors: 'Route 1' Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan (this row) vs 'Route 2' Basra-Haditha-Baniyas (bypasses Kirkuk, goes to Syria instead — out of scope for this candidate). Neither route has been chosen; pipeline-journal explicitly quotes the cabinet describing the agreements as 'strictly exploratory' with 'no immediate financial or contractual obligations,' and peregraf.com quotes oil minister Basim Khudair announcing 'no construction timetable, project cost or guaranteed capacity.' Accordingly: Status=proposed (not construction), FIDStatus=Pre-FID, RouteAccuracy='no route', no Capacity/Length/Diameter/Cost value entered (would overstate certainty this early — an unnamed-official AP figure of ~2 million bpd for the WHOLE corridor system is circulating per peregraf.com/zawya.com but is explicitly not guaranteed and not segment-specific, so left out rather than fabricated-precision).

Separately, a competing/uncoordinated March 2026 Turkish government proposal (Energy Minister Bayraktar, via turkiyetoday.com and zawya.com) to extend Kirkuk-Ceyhan south to Basra is corroborating evidence that BOTH Iraqi and Turkish sides recognize this missing link, but the Turkish side has offered no named sponsor/company and no signed step of its own — it does NOT independently clear the add-threshold and is cited here only as directional corroboration, not as the basis for the row.

Entity check (scripts/entity_lookup.py, --tracker oil): 'Chevron' and 'Basra Oil Company' already exist in the GEM Owner/Parent roster — reused as-is, not restaged. 'Capital TI' and 'UCC Holding' have no close existing match — flagged as genuinely new entities to add to the roster (UCC Holding is the Qatari-Syrian Al-Khayyat-family conglomerate per al-monitor's 'Al-Khayyat brothers' group' description — same entity, different name form used across sources). Ownership percentages are undisclosed anywhere — listed as plain ';'-joined names per existing-sheet convention for unknown splits (e.g. 'Enbridge; Phillips 66; Plains All American' pattern already in the CSV), no fabricated percentages.

Cost estimates are conflicting and clearly refer to the WHOLE Basra-Ceyhan/Baniyas corridor scheme (not this segment alone) — agbi.com cites '$5 billion project' (with a separately-approved $1.5bn specifically for the already-existing Basra-Haditha segment, P0544), while middleeasteye.net cites '$6bn to $10bn.' Given the disagreement and the fact neither figure isolates the Haditha-Kirkuk piece, Cost is left blank rather than picking one.

Tier: HIGH — the core facts (cabinet approval date, consortium members, two-route framing, exploratory/non-binding nature) are corroborated by 5+ genuinely independent outlets (Iraqi/regional business press, US trade press, Turkish press) with no meaningful contradiction, satisfying confidence_tiers.md's '2+ independent sources agree' bar. All 12 evidence URLs passed scripts/url_verifier.py (200 + expected content). No gem.wiki/globalenergymonitor.org/theodora/wikidot URLs used; no URL fabricated.
